subject.title: sessions.patch has no plugin-ownership check, unlike its sessions.delete sibling

question: Should this public cross-plugin `sessions.patch` ownership bypass be handled through normal narrow bugfix review or security-owned advisory/backport handling first?
rationale: The source evidence supports a narrow fix, but the affected behavior is a stable gateway plugin-isolation boundary, so automation should not choose the disclosure and release-handling path on its own.

options.title: Security-reviewed narrow fix
options.body: Patch `sessions.patch` to reuse the delete ownership invariant and add focused regression coverage after maintainer/security approval.

options.title: Authorize immediate repair PR
options.body: Allow a repair worker to prepare the narrow code/test change now, with maintainer/security review before merge or release.

options.title: Declare asymmetry intentional
options.body: Keep the current behavior only if maintainers explicitly decide admin-scoped plugin-runtime callers may patch foreign sessions and document why delete remains stricter.

recommendation.title: Security-reviewed narrow fix
recommendation.body: Patch `sessions.patch` to reuse the delete ownership invariant and add focused regression coverage after maintainer/security approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent code-history signal on the adjacent archive/delete session mutation boundary and is the best available routing owner for this security-boundary choice.
